title: SC-MT012-SessionHooksEngine

scope.summary:
GOAL: Build Handshake Session Hooks - HANDSHAKE-OWNED, vendor-agnostic hooks on agent-session lifecycle and tool events. OPERATOR FRAMING (2026-07-22): hooks are an engine capability of the wrapper, NOT a passthrough to any vendor CLI's hook system (Claude Code hooks/CLAUDE.md conventions were research input only; --bare launches deliberately skip vendor hooks so Handshake's hooks are the single behavior layer). Operators (and later, governed automations) define hooks once and they fire identically whether the session runs on the Claude lane, Codex lane, ACP lane, or a future open-source lane.

EXPECTED DIFF SHAPE: New module src/backend/handshake_core/src/agent_sessions/hooks.rs (+ storage submodule): HookDefinition { hook_id, version, hook_point, matcher (lane_kind?, role_id?, wp/mt scope?, tool_class? - all optional AND-combined), action, blocking (bool), timeout_ms, fail_mode (FailClosed|FailOpen), enabled, provenance }; SurrealDB-backed hook registry with CRUD API + HTTP routes (pattern: RO MT-081 role registry); a HookDispatcher subscribed to the SC MT-009 SessionEventBus and called synchronously at blocking hook points.

HOOK POINTS (v1 catalogue): SessionStart (blocking capable - can veto launch), TurnStart, SteerDelivered, ToolCallRequested (blocking - runs BEFORE SessionToolGate policy evaluation completes, may contribute Deny; never may widen an MT-011 Deny to Allow), ToolCallCompleted, SignalReceived (hsk.mt_signal@1 arrivals), SessionEnd, MergeProposed (WM MT-145 seam). ACTIONS (v1): RunCommand (executes inside a sandbox adapter with the session's workspace scope, output captured + ledgered, hard timeout), EmitEvent (publish typed event to bus + FR), HttpCallback (POST to operator-configured local endpoint, bounded body, no external hosts by default), Decision (blocking points only: Continue | Block(reason)).

SEMANTICS: blocking hooks run in registration order with a per-hook timeout; FailClosed hook timeout/error = Block at blocking points; FailOpen = Continue with a typed warning event; non-blocking hooks run async off the bus with lag protection (HBR-SWARM-002 no-silent-loss - overflow is a typed SubscriberLagged event, never a dropped hook without record). Every hook firing is ledgered (hook_id, point, decision, duration). Hooks NEVER execute with wider filesystem scope than the session's workspace; RunCommand rides the sandbox adapters.

STEP-BY-STEP IMPLEMENTATION:
1. Read SC MT-009 (SessionEventBus + event types) and MT-011 (ToolGate) contracts + code; enumerate the concrete bus events backing each hook point.
2. Define HookDefinition/HookPoint/HookAction/HookDecision types + serde + JSON schema (hsk.session_hook@1); SurrealKit SCHEMAFULL SurrealQL rollout for the registry (additive).
3. Implement registry CRUD (Rust API + axum routes + IPC read) with ledgered mutations, versioning, enable/disable.
4. Implement HookDispatcher: synchronous invocation path for blocking points (SessionStart, ToolCallRequested) wired into the session launch path (SC MT-007) and the MT-011 gate pipeline (hook may add Deny, never override gate Deny); async path for non-blocking points off the bus.
5. Implement actions: RunCommand via sandbox adapter with workspace-scoped mounts + timeout + output capture; EmitEvent; HttpCallback (localhost/allowlist only by default); Decision plumbing.
6. Recording: FR events per firing (RD MT-161 kinds), ledger rows, hook outcomes visible in the RD MT-166 audit surface join.
7. Tests: ordering, timeout fail-closed vs fail-open, blocking veto at SessionStart and ToolCallRequested, no-widen-gate-deny invariant, async lag handling, sandbox scope containment for RunCommand.
forbidden_paths: src/frontend/** (hook management GUI is a later surface; registry ships API-first)
acceptance_criteria: hsk.session_hook@1 registry with CRUD, versioning, enable/disable; mutations ledgered.
All v1 hook points fire from real session events; blocking points (SessionStart, ToolCallRequested) can veto with typed Block(reason).
A hook can contribute Deny at ToolCallRequested but can NEVER convert an MT-011 gate Deny into Allow (invariant test).
FailClosed timeout blocks; FailOpen timeout continues with a typed warning event; both proven.
RunCommand executes inside a sandbox adapter scoped to the session workspace with hard timeout and captured, ledgered output; a hook attempting to read outside the workspace fails (containment test).
Non-blocking hooks never stall the session (async off bus); overflow surfaces as typed SubscriberLagged, never silent loss.
The same hook definition fires identically on two different lanes (proven with the fake adapter + one real lane, or typed NEEDS_MANAGED_RESOURCE_PROOF).
No vendor names in hook schema or vocabulary.
proof_targets: cargo test -p handshake_core session_hooks --nocapture 2>&1 | grep -E 'test result: ok'
implementation_notes: OPERATOR FRAMING 2026-07-22: vendor CLI hook systems are intentionally NOT used (interactive presets favor bare/deterministic launches); Handshake hooks are the one behavior layer so hooks survive vendor swaps.
Hook points map to SC MT-009 bus events; if a needed event is missing, extend the bus event enum there (additive) rather than inventing a parallel channel.
HttpCallback default allowlist = localhost only; external endpoints require explicit operator config (SSRF discipline consistent with existing LlmError SSRF guards).
MergeProposed hook point binds to WM MT-145 merge events via the bus; if WM lands later, the point registers but has no publisher yet (typed inactive, not an error).
Cron-scheduled sessions (SC MT-013) fire the same SessionStart hooks - no special path.

gui_obligation.not_applicable_reason: API-first registry; hook firings surface in the RD MT-166 audit pane; dedicated hook-management GUI is deferred headroom scope.

target_entries: Dexterity session hooks: points, actions, blocking semantics, fail modes
Writing a safe RunCommand hook (workspace scope, timeouts)

risk_if_missed: Automation around sessions stays vendor-coupled (or nonexistent): behaviors like pre-launch checks, tool-call tripwires, and completion side-effects would have to be reimplemented per vendor CLI, breaking the engine-wrapper promise.

risks: RISK-1: A hook RunCommand becomes an unsandboxed code-execution primitive with repo-wide scope.
RISK-2: A hook silently widens tool permissions (Allow where the gate said Deny).
RISK-3: Blocking hooks stall every session (timeout missing or unbounded).
RISK-4: Async hook loss goes unnoticed (dropped events, no record).
RISK-5: HttpCallback exfiltrates session data to arbitrary external hosts.
minimum_controls: CTRL-1 (RISK-1): RunCommand only via sandbox adapters with session-workspace scope + hard timeout; containment test mandatory.
CTRL-2 (RISK-2): Gate-deny is final; hooks may only add Deny - invariant enforced in the dispatcher and covered by a dedicated test.
CTRL-3 (RISK-3): timeout_ms mandatory on every blocking hook; FailClosed/FailOpen explicit; both paths tested.
CTRL-4 (RISK-4): SubscriberLagged typed events + ledger rows for every firing; loss is always visible.
CTRL-5 (RISK-5): localhost/allowlist default for HttpCallback; external hosts require explicit operator config; bounded body size.

research_provenance.source: Operator vendor-agnostic-engine directive 2026-07-22 (hooks are Handshake capabilities, not vendor passthrough); Claude Code hooks taxonomy from the 2026-07-21 research pass as prior art (SessionStart/Stop/PreToolUse shapes) - concept only; SC MT-009 bus + MT-011 gate as the delivery seams.

surrealdb_authority_v02_205.supersedes: Any PostgreSQL, Postgres, PgPool, sqlx-postgres, SQL-DDL, JSONB, RLS, LISTEN-NOTIFY, pgvector, DATABASE_URL, PostgreSQL test-container, or PostgreSQL proof instruction elsewhere in this pre-pivot contract.
surrealdb_authority_v02_205.implementation_rule: When this MT reads or writes durable product state it MUST use the typed SurrealDB boundary created by MT-331..MT-334 and the authenticated record-user plus ResourceBroker privacy contract from MT-333. It MUST NOT add a PostgreSQL fallback, parallel authority, direct pool escape, or runtime dependency.
surrealdb_authority_v02_205.proof_rule: PostgreSQL-era fixtures and historical receipts do not prove this MT. Fresh real-SurrealDB proof is required for every storage-affected acceptance criterion; administrative SurrealDB credentials cannot prove privacy.
surrealdb_authority_v02_205.postgresql_data_migration: NOT_REQUIRED: the current PostgreSQL database contains no valuable live information. No MT may connect to it, import from it, fall back to it, or use it as proof.

surrealdb_translation_v02_205.schema_rule: Any embedded PostgreSQL DDL/SQL snippet is a semantic field/index/invariant inventory only. Implement it as SCHEMAFULL SurrealQL through SurrealKit; do not execute or mechanically transliterate the snippet.
surrealdb_translation_v02_205.concurrency_rule: Translate advisory locks, SKIP LOCKED and row locks into SurrealDB transactions, durable lease/fencing records and conditional updates with equivalent tests.
surrealdb_translation_v02_205.notification_rule: Translate LISTEN/NOTIFY into scoped SurrealDB live queries plus bounded resynchronization.
surrealdb_translation_v02_205.privacy_rule: Translate RLS into authenticated record-user table/field PERMISSIONS intersected with ResourceBroker; administrative credentials cannot prove privacy.
surrealdb_translation_v02_205.proof_rule: All named storage proofs run against real SurrealDB. No PostgreSQL process, driver, connection, fixture, environment variable or fallback is permitted.
